bull.b: LOQTORZI is showing measurable commercial traction, with sequential sales growth, more new patient starts, and improving treatment duration. If quarterly growth continues, the product can become a more meaningful recurring revenue base and support Coherus’s transition toward a focused oncology business.

Sustained reductions in R&D and SG&A indicate improving cost discipline rather than a single-quarter action. A leaner operating structure can extend funding capacity, reduce the revenue threshold for eventual profitability, and give management more flexibility to prioritize oncology development.

Completion of enrollment across key clinical programs advances Coherus toward important efficacy and safety readouts. A maturing oncology pipeline can diversify future growth beyond current commercial sales and create additional opportunities if the studies confirm the early activity signals.

bear.b: The company is not currently self-funding operations, as substantial operating and free-cash-flow losses consume financial resources. Continued burn increases dependence on cost reductions, asset monetization, debt, or equity financing and leaves less flexibility to absorb setbacks in commercialization or clinical development.

The sharp historical revenue decline and modest current scale indicate an unstable earnings foundation. Even with recent top-line improvement, Coherus must successfully expand LOQTORZI and future products to offset lost biosimilar revenue and achieve operating leverage on its substantial cost base.

Key oncology value drivers still depend on immature data that may change after cleaning and longer follow-up, while commercial adoption has operational friction. These issues could delay validation of the pipeline or slow product uptake, extending the period before the business reaches sustainable scale.
